#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

find_mathc() {
  if [ -n "${MATHC:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${MATHC}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v mathc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v mathc
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

need_mathc() {
  mathc_bin="$(find_mathc)" || {
    echo "scripts/dev $cmd: mathc is not on PATH and MATHC is not set." >&2
    echo "  Get it from the math-coding repository: nix build  (it writes result/bin/mathc)." >&2
    exit 3
  }
}

# Emacs loads a byte-compiled file when it exists, even when the source is
# newer ("Source file ... newer than byte-compiled file; using older file").
# A stale .elc next to a modified source therefore makes every check test
# yesterday's code instead of today's. The bytecode is a build artifact, not
# a part of the tree: it is removed before anything is loaded.
clean_bytecode() {
  rm -f lib/*.elc bench/*.elc
}

now_ms() {
  printf '%s' "$(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000000 ))"
}

case "$cmd" in
  help|--help|-h)
    cat <<'EOF'
scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper

Subcommands:
  smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
  byte-compile-all      — byte-compile lib/*.el (including lib/yeah.el), no warnings
  ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
  bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
  pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
  map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
  run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
  gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
  help                  — this text

Exit codes:
  0 — pass       (Green)
  1 — fail       (Red)
  2 — blocked    (input error)
  3 — unknown    (the method could not tell)

Environment:
  MATHC  — path to the math-coding binary (default: `mathc` on PATH)
  EMACS  — path to the Emacs binary (default: `emacs` on PATH)
EOF
    ;;

  smoke)

    exit 0

;;; check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el --- the check of the bridge decides the race by construction -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The check of the bridge used to race the subject: it kept a thread
;; spinning to make the parent late, read the buffer of the attached
;; Emacs a hundred and twenty times, and failed only when the answer
;; was really lost.  Five runs of six bit and one did not (2026-11-16):
;; the claim of the bridge came out `inconclusive' and the map came
;; out `unknown'.  An evidence that decides its verdict by a race
;; cannot be read.
;;
;; This check is the evidence of that repair.  It takes the control of
;; the claim of the bridge — the drain of the bridge removed — and runs
;; the check of the bridge against it ten times in a copy of the
;; repository.  Every one of the ten runs must fail by an assertion of
;; the check: the same code, the same verdict, ten times in a row.  A
;; run that crashes Emacs, a run that hangs and a run that passes are
;; all failures of this check.
;;
;; The check of the bridge must also pass on the whole bridge, before
;; the control is applied: a check that fails whatever the subject does
;; proves nothing.

;;; Code:

(require 'json)
(require 'seq)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the check of the bridge.")

(defvar yeah-check--root
  (or (locate-dominating-file (or load-file-name buffer-file-name default-directory)
                              "spec.json")
      default-directory)
  "The root of the repository: the directory that holds `spec.json'.
The check knows where it is by the specification it reads, and not by
the depth of its own file.")

(defvar yeah-check--runs 10
  "How many consecutive runs of the control the claim of the bridge asks for.")

(defvar yeah-check--run-timeout 120
  "Seconds a run of the check of the bridge may take.")

(defconst yeah-check--bridge-check "tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el"
  "The check of the bridge, the one this check runs.")

(defun yeah-check--field (object key)
  "Return the value of the field KEY of OBJECT, or nil when it has none.
The keys of a JSON object come as symbols from Emacs 30 and as strings
from the older Emacs: the check asks for both and finds the field
whichever way the specification was read."
  (and (listp object)
       (or (alist-get key object)
           (alist-get (symbol-name key) object nil #'string=))))

(defun yeah-check--control-of (claim-id)

# PLAN — the road to Yeah 1.0

> **Status: execution plan, not current capability.** The target and its
> rationale are in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; binding engineering rules are in
> `docs/ENGINEERING.md`. The machine-checked present is `spec.json` and
> `./scripts/dev map`.
>
> This plan introduces eight **stages**. Existing `waves/wave-01.json` …
> `wave-14.json` remain the historical math-coding units until corresponding
> new claims/waves are added. A stage is not considered closed here: closure
> requires the specification and its evidence to agree.

## 1. Current baseline

Verified on 2026-11-15 on `main` (the numbers of 2026-11-14 in the integration
branch were 319/319, 46 and 55):

- all 53 Elisp files under `lib/` byte-compile without warnings;
- 358/358 ERT unit tests pass;
- all 53 canaries pass when run directly (`./scripts/dev check tests/checks/*`);
- the installed math-coding v5 tool runs the standing specification: all 74
  claims hold, and every negative control changes its scoped subject and
  makes the verifier fail with an assertion;
- live provider behavior remains verified on 2026-11-12: the live coding task
  (MiniMax-M3.1-Flash) reads the project, edits the file with a guarded edit,
  saves it, and the test of the project passes, and the interactive UI
  path (journal, cancel, quit, restart, resume, recover) works against a
  live provider.  The clean-Emacs install path is network-tested against the
  published repository (`tests/live/live-clean-install.el`).

The code contains a working kernel and a working wire, but not yet a usable
product:

- the stdio wire server answers one request at a time: a cancel that
  arrives while a prompt runs is read after that prompt settles.  The
  socket transport (`lib/yeah-wire-socket.el`) does not have this limit —
  a cancel arrives while the prompt is still running;
- the emacsclient bridge was checked against a live Emacs server (a real
  daemon) by `tests/checks/check-bridge-live-server.el`, but not yet against
  a person's Emacs in day-to-day use;
- concurrent sessions in one Emacs are isolated per run context: sessions,
  permissions, cancellation, budgets and the advertised tools are the run's
  own, and two sessions in one Emacs are checked for cross-talk;
- the PTC whitelist was experimentally bypassed with a permitted higher-order
  function and a quoted `delete-file` symbol. It is not a safe boundary.

## 2. Stage map and dependencies

```text
0. Honesty and safety
   └─> 1. Coding tools
         └─> 2. Context and compaction
               └─> 3. Human control
                     └─> 4. Installable interactive product  [PUBLIC ALPHA]
                           └─> 5. ACP/MCP wire
                                 └─> 6. Placements
                                       └─> 7. Delegation and ecosystem

Benchmarks and documentation run continuously; 1.0 requires stages 0–7 and
release gates from §11.
```

ACP and service mode come after the interactive slice deliberately: they
must transport a working kernel, not conceal missing execution behind
protocol handlers.  Minimal Emacs-native UI and installation come before
them because they validate the actual user experience.

**Primary deployment path (decided 2026-11-12).**  The practical main use
of Yeah is the service placement: a dedicated Emacs process runs the
harness, because the person's editing Emacs is single-threaded and an
in-editor agent would block editing.  The editor reaches the harness
through the emacsclient bridge; external clients and orchestrators (an
ACP client such as agent-shell, or an orchestrator such as Paseo) speak
ACP or MCP to the same service.  The attached `M-x yeah` placement
remains the demo, development and fallback path.

This decision does not reorder the stages; it re-prices their exit
criteria.  A cancel that preempts a running prompt on the wire, a bridge
verified against a live Emacs server, concurrent sessions in one service
Emacs and bounded CPU work inside the agent process are release-relevant

(a human review, not a machine verifier), and this section is the plan that
the decision refers to.  The order is by the price of the defect: the wave
that makes the verdict of the method unreadable goes first, and the wave that
opens the path from a model to a working program goes last.

The order of the next waves, named by the owner on 2026-11-16: **wave 41, wave 42, wave 43, wave 44.**

They are: wave 41 (the deterministic verifier of the bridge), wave 42 (the
process of the server), wave 43 (the surface of ACP for an orchestrator), wave
44 (parallel children in a live turn).

One wave was executed before them: **wave 45** (2026-11-17), the repair of
the harness that the live test of the harness forced — a tool that returns
bytes that are not text took the whole Emacs process down, and the four
waves of this plan need a harness that lives to carry them (§16.24).  The
order named by the owner is unchanged: wave 41 is still the first of the
four.

Every wave below names the defect it removes, the claims it registers, the
control that has to bite, and the criteria that close it.  A wave that ends
without a control that bites is not a wave: it is a change of the code with
no evidence.

### 18.1 Wave 41 — the verifier of the bridge decides the race by construction

**The defect.**  One verifier of the standing specification is a race.  The
check of `bridge-keeps-the-answer` reads the buffer of an attached Emacs a
hundred and twenty times while a thread keeps the parent late, and it fails
only when the answer is really lost.  Six runs of the evidence on 2026-11-16:
five bit, one did not — the control reached the subject, the verifier after
the control still passed, the claim came out `inconclusive`, and the map came
out `unknown`.  The code was not the cause of that verdict; the evidence was.

**Why this wave is first.**  Every other wave of this plan ends with a run
of the method, and a run whose verdict depends on a race may say `unknown`
for a reason that has nothing to do with the code it names.  A map that says
`unknown` because of a race cannot be read.

**What changes.**  The check stops racing the subject and starts commanding
it: the loss of the answer becomes a condition that the check arranges — a
barrier the parent waits for, a hook the check owns — so that the same
input gives the same verdict every time.  The control of the claim becomes
the same arrangement with one step removed, and the check must then fail by
its own assertion.

**The claims.**
- `bridge-keeps-the-answer` — the existing claim, re-bound with a control
  that bites every time (register `fact`, requirement: the check of the
  bridge).
- `the-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction` — a new claim: the
  check of the bridge gives the same verdict on ten consecutive runs of the
  control, and the control bites on each of them (register `fact`).

**The exit criteria.**
1. Ten consecutive runs of the control bite: every one of them fails by an
   assertion of the check, not by a crash of Emacs and not by a timeout.
2. Two consecutive runs of the method end in `green`, with no `inconclusive`
   claim and no `unknown` verdict.

**The estimate.**  Half a day to a day.  **What this wave does not fix.**  It
repairs the evidence, not the harness: nothing of the run itself changes.

### 18.2 Wave 42 — the server does not outlive the agent, and it does not spin

**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP
server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open
after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.
And some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace:
one of them was measured with 1,921,354 involuntary context switches and six
voluntary ones — it never slept — at 25–60 % of a core.

**What is known and what is not.**  The read loop of the server is not the
cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,
and a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four
per cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request of
the provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet: `ptrace` and `strace`
are not available in this environment ("Operation not permitted"), so the
localization has to be done by measurement — the ticks of `/proc/<pid>/stat`,
not the percentage of the CPU that `top` prints.

**What changes.**
1. *The life cycle.*  The server has a way to end that does not depend on the
   client closing the pipe: the session ends, and the process exits.  The
   plugin of Paseo (`yeah-provider`, outside this repository) closes the pipe
   of the server when the session of the agent is over; the kernel side gives
   it a way to say so.
2. *The spin.*  The loop on the path of the live request is localized by
   instrumentation — a counter of the iterations of the pump and of the
   request of the provider — measured the way the defect itself was measured.
   The loop that spins is then removed, and the bound becomes a check.

**The claims.**
- `the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over` — the process of the server is
  gone after the session ends, even when the client keeps the pipe open
  (the control keeps the pipe open and ends the session: the check must
  fail).
- `the-server-does-not-spin-when-the-provider-is-silent` — a server whose
  provider went silent costs less than one per cent of a core over ten
  seconds (the control brings the busy loop back: the measured ticks must
  exceed the bound).

**The exit criteria.**
1. A server left behind by a finished session is gone within ten seconds.
2. The ticks of a silent server stay under the bound in ten consecutive
   measurements.
3. The live check of the plugin leaves no process behind.

**The estimate.**  One to two days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  A
transport that dies with "Curl failed with exit code 28" is the provider's
death, not the harness's.

### 18.3 Wave 43 — the surface of ACP that an orchestrator needs

**The defect.**  The integration with Paseo found four gaps of the surface,
and all of them point the same way: an orchestrator cannot put the agent
where the work is, cannot change what the agent may do, and cannot read what
the agent did.

;;; check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el --- the check of the bridge decides the race by construction -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The check of the bridge used to race the subject: it kept a thread
;; spinning to make the parent late, read the buffer of the attached
;; Emacs a hundred and twenty times, and failed only when the answer
;; was really lost.  Five runs of six bit and one did not (2026-11-16):
;; the claim of the bridge came out `inconclusive' and the map came
;; out `unknown'.  An evidence that decides its verdict by a race
;; cannot be read.
;;
;; This check is the evidence of that repair.  It takes the control of
;; the claim of the bridge — the drain of the bridge removed — and runs
;; the check of the bridge against it ten times in a copy of the
;; repository.  Every one of the ten runs must fail by an assertion of
;; the check: the same code, the same verdict, ten times in a row.  A
;; run that crashes Emacs, a run that hangs and a run that passes are
;; all failures of this check.
;;
;; The check of the bridge must also pass on the whole bridge, before
;; the control is applied: a check that fails whatever the subject does
;; proves nothing.

;;; Code:

(require 'json)
(require 'seq)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the check of the bridge.")

(defvar yeah-check--root
  (or (locate-dominating-file (or load-file-name buffer-file-name default-directory)
                              "spec.json")
      default-directory)
  "The root of the repository: the directory that holds `spec.json'.
The check knows where it is by the specification it reads, and not by
the depth of its own file.")

(defvar yeah-check--runs 10
  "How many consecutive runs of the control the claim of the bridge asks for.")

(defvar yeah-check--run-timeout 120
  "Seconds a run of the check of the bridge may take.")

(defconst yeah-check--bridge-check "tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el"
  "The check of the bridge, the one this check runs.")

(defun yeah-check--field (object key)
  "Return the value of the field KEY of OBJECT, or nil when it has none.
The keys of a JSON object come as symbols from Emacs 30 and as strings
from the older Emacs: the check asks for both and finds the field
whichever way the specification was read."
  (and (listp object)
       (or (alist-get key object)
           (alist-get (symbol-name key) object nil #'string=))))

(defun yeah-check--control-of (claim-id)
  "Return the control of the claim CLAIM-ID, or nil when it has none.
The control is read from the standing specification: the check runs
the control that the claim declares, and not a copy of it."
  (let* ((json-object-type 'alist)
         (spec (json-read-file (expand-file-name "spec.json" yeah-check--root)))
         (claims (yeah-check--field spec 'claims))
         (claim (seq-find (lambda (entry) (equal (yeah-check--field entry 'id)
                                                 claim-id))
                           claims)))
    (and claim (yeah-check--field claim 'control))))

(defun yeah-check--copy-tree (source target)
  "Copy the tree of the directory SOURCE into the directory TARGET."
  (make-directory target t)
  (dolist (entry (directory-files source t directory-files-no-dot-files-regexp t))
    (let ((name (file-name-nondirectory entry)))
      (if (file-directory-p entry)
          (yeah-check--copy-tree entry (expand-file-name name target))
        (copy-file entry (expand-file-name name target))))))

(defun yeah-check--bridge-command (directory)
  "Return the command that runs the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY."
  (list yeah-check--emacs "-Q" "--batch"
        "-L" (expand-file-name "lib" directory)
        "-L" directory
        "-l" (expand-file-name yeah-check--bridge-check directory)))

(defun yeah-check--run-bridge-check (directory)
  "Run the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY.
Return the code of the run and the words it printed.  The code of a
run that did not finish in time is the symbol `timeout'."
  (let* ((output "")
         (words (generate-new-buffer " *yeah-bridge-check words*"))
         (process (make-process
                    :name "yeah-bridge-check-run"
                    :command (yeah-check--bridge-command directory)
                    :connection-type 'pipe
                    :noquery t
                    :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                    :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                              (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                    :stderr words)))
    (unwind-protect
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) yeah-check--run-timeout)))
          (while (and (process-live-p process)
                      (< (float-time) deadline))
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (if (process-live-p process)
              (progn
                (ignore-errors (kill-process process))
                (cons 'timeout output))
            (cons (process-exit-status process)
                  (concat output (with-current-buffer words (buffer-string))))))
      (when (buffer-live-p words)
        (kill-buffer words)))))

(defun yeah-check--apply-control (control directory)
  "Run the shell command CONTROL in DIRECTORY and return its code."
  (let ((process (make-process
                  :name "yeah-bridge-control"
                  :command (list "sh" "-c"
                                 (format "cd %s && %s"
                                         (shell-quote-argument directory)
                                         control))
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8))))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (while (process-live-p process)
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (process-exit-status process))
      (when (process-live-p process)
        (ignore-errors (kill-process process))))))

(defun yeah-check--failures ()
  "Run the check of the bridge against the control of the claim.
Return the list of the failures of the check."
  (let ((failures nil)
        (control (yeah-check--control-of "bridge-keeps-the-answer"))
        (directory (make-temp-file "yeah-bridge-control-" t)))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (if (null control)
              (push "the claim of the bridge declares no control to run" failures)
            (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name "lib" yeah-check--root)
                                   (expand-file-name "lib" directory))
            (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name "tests" yeah-check--root)
                                   (expand-file-name "tests" directory))
            ;; the check of the bridge passes on the whole bridge
            (let ((run (yeah-check--run-bridge-check yeah-check--root)))
              (unless (eq (car run) 0)
                (push (format "the check of the bridge does not pass on the whole bridge: %S"
                              (car run))
                      failures)))
            ;; the control of the claim, and ten runs of the check against it
            (let ((code (yeah-check--apply-control control directory)))
              (unless (eq code 0)
                (push (format "the control of the claim of the bridge did not apply: %S"
                              code)
                      failures)))
            (dotimes (run yeah-check--runs)
              (let* ((result (yeah-check--run-bridge-check directory))
                     (code (car result))
                     (words (cdr result)))
                (cond
                 ((eq code 'timeout)
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control did not finish in %d seconds"
                                (1+ run) yeah-check--run-timeout)
                        failures))
                 ((not (eq code 1))
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control ended with the code %S: the control did not bite by an assertion"
                                (1+ run) code)
                        failures))
                 ((not (string-match-p "bridge-keep:" words))
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control did not fail by an assertion of the check: %S"
                                (1+ run) words)
                        failures)))))))
      (when (file-directory-p directory)
        (delete-directory directory t)))
    failures))

(let ((failures (yeah-check--failures)))
  (dolist (failure failures)
    (message "bridge-race: %s" failure))
  (if failures
      (kill-emacs 1)
    (kill-emacs 0)))

;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el --- the bridge does not lose the answer -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The bridge collects what the attached Emacs printed with a process
;; filter.  A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the
;; filter: the answer was then lost and the bridge reported success
;; with an empty output — the person saw an empty buffer that the
;; server had never emptied.
;;
;; The check used to race the subject: it kept a thread spinning to
;; make the parent late, read the buffer of the attached Emacs a
;; hundred and twenty times and failed only when the answer was
;; really lost.  Five runs of six bit and one did not (2026-11-16):
;; the claim came out `inconclusive' and the map came out `unknown'.
;; The check now commands the subject instead of racing it.  The
;; hooks it owns hold the answer of the child process until the
;; bridge asks for the pending output of a process that is gone —
;; the very condition of the defect — and the bridge must deliver
;; the answer all the same.  The same input gives the same verdict
;; every time, and the control of the claim (the drain of the bridge
;; removed) makes the check fail by its own assertion.

;;; Code:

(require 'yeah-bridge)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--emacsclient
  (let* ((dir (file-name-directory yeah-check--emacs))
         (candidate (expand-file-name "emacsclient" dir)))
    (or (and (file-executable-p candidate) candidate)
        (executable-find "emacsclient")
        candidate))
  "The emacsclient program that reaches the server.")

(defconst yeah-check--answer "live text"
  "The text the attached Emacs holds in the buffer of the check.")

(defvar yeah-check--hold-the-answer t
  "Whether the check holds the answer of the child until the bridge drains it.
The control of the claim of the determinism removes this one step: the
check then reads the buffer as it always did, the loss of the answer
is a race again, and the control of the bridge does not bite.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-chunk nil
  "The chunk of the child process that the filter has not delivered yet.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-filter nil
  "The filter of the bridge, kept to deliver the held chunk later.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-process nil
  "The process of the bridge, kept to deliver the held chunk later.")

(defun yeah-check--filter-of (args)
  "Return the filter of ARGS, or nil when ARGS names none."
  (let ((tail args)
        (filter nil))
    (while tail
      (when (eq (car tail) :filter)
        (setq filter (cadr tail)))
      (setq tail (cddr tail)))
    filter))

(defun yeah-check--without-filter (args)
  "Return ARGS without the :filter keyword and its value."
  (let ((rest nil)
        (tail args))
    (while tail
      (unless (eq (car tail) :filter)
        (setq rest (append rest (list (car tail) (cadr tail)))))
      (setq tail (cddr tail)))
    rest))

(defun yeah-check--around-make-process (orig-fun &rest args)
  "Create the process of the bridge, but hold what it prints.
The filter of the process keeps the chunk instead of handing it to
the bridge: the answer of the child reaches the bridge only when the
bridge asks for the pending output of a process that is gone."
  (let ((filter (yeah-check--filter-of args)))
    (if (and filter yeah-check--hold-the-answer)
        (progn
          (setq yeah-check--held-filter filter)
          (let ((process
                 (apply orig-fun
                        (append (yeah-check--without-filter args)
                                (list :filter
                                      (lambda (_process chunk)
                                        (setq yeah-check--held-chunk
                                              (concat yeah-check--held-chunk
                                                      chunk))))))))
            (setq yeah-check--held-process process)
            process))
      (apply orig-fun args))))

(defun yeah-check--around-accept-process-output (orig-fun &optional process &rest args)
  "Run the event loop of Emacs, and give the held answer to the bridge.
The answer of the child is delivered when the bridge asks for the
pending output of a process that is gone: the bridge reads the answer
of the child after its exit, which is the condition the defect is
about."
  (let ((result (apply orig-fun process (or args (list 0.05)))))
    (when (and yeah-check--hold-the-answer
               (null process)
               yeah-check--held-chunk
               yeah-check--held-filter)
      (let ((chunk yeah-check--held-chunk))
        (setq yeah-check--held-chunk nil)
        (funcall yeah-check--held-filter yeah-check--held-process chunk)))
    result))

(defun yeah-check--advise (symbol function)
  "Advise SYMBOL with FUNCTION.
Emacs 30 asks for the kind of the advice and the older Emacs does
not; the advice itself takes the original function as its first
argument in both."
  (if (>= emacs-major-version 30)
      (advice-add symbol :around function)
    (advice-add symbol function)))

(let ((failures nil)
      (name (format "yeah-bridge-keep-%d" (random 1000000))))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        (make-process
         :name "yeah-bridge-keep-server"
         :command (list yeah-check--emacs
                        (concat "--daemon=" name)
                        "--eval"
                        (format (concat "(with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create \"*yeah-live*\") "
                                        "(insert \"%s\"))")
                                yeah-check--answer))
         :connection-type 'pipe
         :noquery t)
        ;; wait for the server
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) 8)))
          (while (and (< (float-time) deadline)
                      (not (zerop (with-temp-buffer
                                    (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil
                                                  "-s" name "--eval" "t")))))
            (accept-process-output nil 0.1)))
        ;; the hooks of the check: the answer of the child waits for the
        ;; bridge to ask for the pending output of a process that is gone
        (yeah-check--advise 'make-process #'yeah-check--around-make-process)
        (yeah-check--advise 'accept-process-output
                            #'yeah-check--around-accept-process-output)
        (unwind-protect
            (let ((text (condition-case err
                           (let ((yeah-bridge-program yeah-check--emacsclient)
                                 (yeah-bridge-server name))
                             (yeah-bridge-buffer-read "*yeah-live*"))
                         (error (format "ERROR: %S" err)))))
              (unless (equal yeah-check--answer text)
                (push (format "the bridge lost the answer: it answered %S" text)
                      failures)))
          (advice-remove 'make-process #'yeah-check--around-make-process)
          (advice-remove 'accept-process-output
                         #'yeah-check--around-accept-process-output)))
    ;; stop the server
    (ignore-errors
      (with-temp-buffer
        (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil "-s" name "--eval" "(kill-emacs)")))
    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "bridge-keep: %s" failure))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el ends here

integration with the orchestrator Paseo.  The decision is recorded by the
method as the judgment claim `the-owner-decided-the-order-of-the-next-waves`
(a human review, not a machine verifier), and this section is the plan that
the decision refers to.  The order is by the price of the defect: the wave
that makes the verdict of the method unreadable goes first, and the wave that
opens the path from a model to a working program goes last.

The order of the next waves, named by the owner on 2026-11-16: **wave 41, wave 42, wave 43, wave 44.**

They are: wave 41 (the deterministic verifier of the bridge), wave 42 (the
process of the server), wave 43 (the surface of ACP for an orchestrator), wave
44 (parallel children in a live turn).

One wave was executed before them: **wave 45** (2026-11-17), the repair of
the harness that the live test of the harness forced — a tool that returns
bytes that are not text took the whole Emacs process down, and the four
waves of this plan need a harness that lives to carry them (§16.24).  The
order named by the owner is unchanged: wave 41 is still the first of the
four.

Every wave below names the defect it removes, the claims it registers, the
control that has to bite, and the criteria that close it.  A wave that ends
without a control that bites is not a wave: it is a change of the code with
no evidence.

### 18.1 Wave 41 — the verifier of the bridge decides the race by construction

**The defect.**  One verifier of the standing specification is a race.  The
check of `bridge-keeps-the-answer` reads the buffer of an attached Emacs a
hundred and twenty times while a thread keeps the parent late, and it fails
only when the answer is really lost.  Six runs of the evidence on 2026-11-16:
five bit, one did not — the control reached the subject, the verifier after
the control still passed, the claim came out `inconclusive`, and the map came
out `unknown`.  The code was not the cause of that verdict; the evidence was.

**Why this wave is first.**  Every other wave of this plan ends with a run
of the method, and a run whose verdict depends on a race may say `unknown`
for a reason that has nothing to do with the code it names.  A map that says
`unknown` because of a race cannot be read.

**What changes.**  The check stops racing the subject and starts commanding
it: the loss of the answer becomes a condition that the check arranges — a
barrier the parent waits for, a hook the check owns — so that the same
input gives the same verdict every time.  The control of the claim becomes
the same arrangement with one step removed, and the check must then fail by
its own assertion.

**The claims.**
- `bridge-keeps-the-answer` — the existing claim, re-bound with a control
  that bites every time (register `fact`, requirement: the check of the
  bridge).
- `the-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction` — a new claim: the
  check of the bridge gives the same verdict on ten consecutive runs of the
  control, and the control bites on each of them (register `fact`).

**The exit criteria.**
1. Ten consecutive runs of the control bite: every one of them fails by an
   assertion of the check, not by a crash of Emacs and not by a timeout.
2. Two consecutive runs of the method end in `green`, with no `inconclusive`
   claim and no `unknown` verdict.

**The estimate.**  Half a day to a day.  **What this wave does not fix.**  It
repairs the evidence, not the harness: nothing of the run itself changes.

### 18.2 Wave 42 — the server does not outlive the agent, and it does not spin

**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP
server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open
after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.
And some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace:
one of them was measured with 1,921,354 involuntary context switches and six
voluntary ones — it never slept — at 25–60 % of a core.

**What is known and what is not.**  The read loop of the server is not the
cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,
and a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four
per cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request of
the provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet: `ptrace` and `strace`
are not available in this environment ("Operation not permitted"), so the
localization has to be done by measurement — the ticks of `/proc/<pid>/stat`,
not the percentage of the CPU that `top` prints.

**What changes.**
1. *The life cycle.*  The server has a way to end that does not depend on the
   client closing the pipe: the session ends, and the process exits.  The
   plugin of Paseo (`yeah-provider`, outside this repository) closes the pipe
   of the server when the session of the agent is over; the kernel side gives
   it a way to say so.
2. *The spin.*  The loop on the path of the live request is localized by
   instrumentation — a counter of the iterations of the pump and of the
   request of the provider — measured the way the defect itself was measured.
   The loop that spins is then removed, and the bound becomes a check.

**The claims.**
- `the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over` — the process of the server is
  gone after the session ends, even when the client keeps the pipe open
  (the control keeps the pipe open and ends the session: the check must
  fail).
- `the-server-does-not-spin-when-the-provider-is-silent` — a server whose
  provider went silent costs less than one per cent of a core over ten
  seconds (the control brings the busy loop back: the measured ticks must
  exceed the bound).

**The exit criteria.**
1. A server left behind by a finished session is gone within ten seconds.
2. The ticks of a silent server stay under the bound in ten consecutive
   measurements.
3. The live check of the plugin leaves no process behind.

**The estimate.**  One to two days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  A
transport that dies with "Curl failed with exit code 28" is the provider's
death, not the harness's.

### 18.3 Wave 43 — the surface of ACP that an orchestrator needs

**The defect.**  The integration with Paseo found four gaps of the surface,
and all of them point the same way: an orchestrator cannot put the agent
where the work is, cannot change what the agent may do, and cannot read what
the agent did.

# AGENTS.md — the entry point to this repository

> **Yeah** means **Yeah, Emacs Agent Harness**: a recursive acronym, the
> **Y** is the Y-combinator. The harness itself is
> Emacs Lisp; Emacs is not merely a client to an external agent. The model is
> reached through gptel, effects go through the tool registry and permission
> system, and session history is append-only JSONL.
>
> The long-term Y metaphor means bounded recursive delegation, runtime
> self-inspection and a fixed point where Yeah can develop and verify Yeah.
> These are goals, not assertions about today's prototype.
>
> This repository is governed by **math-coding v5**: `spec.json` holds the
> standing specification (`schema_version: 5`) and the claims, `waves/*.json`
> holds the historical work units, and evidence comes from checks bound by
> `mathc run`.  Version 4 is frozen and archived at `waves/spec-v4.json`;
> its evidence is not current.
> `docs/PLAN.md` defines the current target sequence; do not mistake an old
> wave number or a green module row for a working end-to-end feature.

## Read first, in this order

1. `README.md` — actual current status and explicit limitations.
2. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the normative target: purpose, ten decisions,
   contracts, security, placements and non-goals.
3. `docs/PLAN.md` — the detailed eight-stage execution plan and release gates.
4. `docs/ENGINEERING.md` — binding dependency, infrastructure, library,
   process, security, testing and packaging practices.
5. `spec.json` — the standing machine-checked specification.
6. `waves/*.json` — existing math-coding units, with intent, check, promise
   and objection.
7. `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md` — kernel Elisp conventions; §11 is the trap log.
8. `lib/yeah-*.el` — the implementation, one feature per file.

If two sources contradict each other, report the contradiction in the open
work item. Never resolve it by silently making documentation more optimistic.

## Current warnings for every agent

- This is a kernel prototype, not a usable coding product.
- The parity with other harnesses was piloted on 2026-11-15, and the
  difference the pilot found was a defect of the turn, not a difference of
  quality: after the results of the tool calls arrive, the model may answer
  with an empty message, and the turn took that as the end of the work and
  stopped without the effect (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The pilot of the
  parity").  The defect is fixed (the claim
  `an-empty-answer-does-not-end-the-run'), and the pilot on the fixed turn
  moved one task of three; the nudge now carries the state of the work

is blocked tooling, not a successful check.

Exit codes are: `0` pass, `1` fail, `2` blocked/input error and `3` unknown.

## The method

Start with the map when the compatible method binary is available:

```sh
./scripts/dev map
```

A claim has a scope, requirement, falsifier, register and **control**. The
control breaks the subject and must make the check fail by a real assertion,
not merely by making the test unreadable or crashing Emacs. A claim whose
control has not bitten is not established.

Two rules are not negotiable:

- **A check that cannot fail is a comment.**
- **Unknown is not pass.**

A placeholder that returns success is also a failed implementation. Public
scenarios must be tested end to end, not inferred from the presence of a
function or module.

Yeah is an Emacs Lisp agent harness: the harness runs in a dedicated Emacs process (the service placement); the model goes through gptel, every tool goes through the registry and the permission system, the session log stays append-only, and the editor reaches it through the bridge or an ACP/MCP client

## Task recording for the Math Coding field pilot

This project takes part in a measurement of the method itself. A task that ends
with a handoff is recorded in the field lab; without that record the pilot has
no data and the method cannot be judged.

At the end of the task, create a draft — the machine fields are filled for you:

```sh
~/Projects/math-coding-field-lab/scripts/record draft yeah --kind <kind> --base <revision-at-task-start>
```

Fill the fields marked `TODO`: the model, the time, the counters. Leave `outcome`
as `pending` and `accepted_by` empty — the owner decides the outcome and records
the acceptance, and that is not the agent's call. Then write the record:

```sh
~/Projects/math-coding-field-lab/scripts/record commit yeah --task-id <id>
```

Rules: do not choose tasks by their result, do not rewrite a written record to
make it look better, and do not drop unsuccessful ones — the pilot publishes
every outcome. The lab records every task that starts after the declared rule:
it never stops asking and it never filters by result. If the lab is not
available, finish the task as usual: a missing record is a gap in the
measurement, not a reason to change the work.

## Working rules

- Follow the stage order in `docs/PLAN.md`; do not start ACP, placements or
  sub-agents ahead of their prerequisites.
- Every new claim needs a control shown to bite. Every feature needs an
  observable end-to-end check appropriate to its layer.
- `lib/` is Elisp only. No C, Rust or shell scripts inside the kernel.
- One feature per file; `(require 'yeah-x)` loads `lib/yeah-x.el`.
- Public symbols use `yeah-`; internal helpers use `yeah--` or the module's
  established internal prefix.
- Domain errors are `user-error` or structured tool errors, not false success.
- Use `let` for request-local dynamic configuration of special variables;
  use `setq` only for intended global/session mutation. See ELISP §11.1.
- Subprocesses use `make-process`, never blocking `shell-command` in tools.
- Interactive execution never waits by spinning the event loop.
- Run context, permissions and sessions must not leak through new global
  mutable state.
- No telemetry, secret logging, global default keybindings or global gptel
  mutation.
- Development-only Nix/mathc/research clones never become runtime dependencies.

The detailed rationale and additional rules are in `docs/ENGINEERING.md` and
`ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md`. Update documentation whenever behavior changes;
update `AGENTS.md` if the documented workflow itself changes.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

find_mathc() {
  if [ -n "${MATHC:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${MATHC}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v mathc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v mathc
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

need_mathc() {
  mathc_bin="$(find_mathc)" || {
    echo "scripts/dev $cmd: mathc is not on PATH and MATHC is not set." >&2
    echo "  Get it from the math-coding repository: nix build  (it writes result/bin/mathc)." >&2
    exit 3
  }
}

# Emacs loads a byte-compiled file when it exists, even when the source is
# newer ("Source file ... newer than byte-compiled file; using older file").
# A stale .elc next to a modified source therefore makes every check test
# yesterday's code instead of today's. The bytecode is a build artifact, not
# a part of the tree: it is removed before anything is loaded.
clean_bytecode() {
  rm -f lib/*.elc bench/*.elc
}

;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el --- the bridge does not lose the answer -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The bridge collects what the attached Emacs printed with a process
;; filter.  A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the
;; filter: the answer was then lost and the bridge reported success
;; with an empty output — the person saw an empty buffer that the
;; server had never emptied.
;;
;; The check used to race the subject: it kept a thread spinning to
;; make the parent late, read the buffer of the attached Emacs a
;; hundred and twenty times and failed only when the answer was
;; really lost.  Five runs of six bit and one did not (2026-11-16):
;; the claim came out `inconclusive' and the map came out `unknown'.
;; The check now commands the subject instead of racing it.  The
;; hooks it owns hold the answer of the child process until the
;; bridge asks for the pending output of a process that is gone —
;; the very condition of the defect — and the bridge must deliver
;; the answer all the same.  The same input gives the same verdict
;; every time, and the control of the claim (the drain of the bridge
;; removed) makes the check fail by its own assertion.

;;; Code:

(require 'yeah-bridge)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--emacsclient
  (let* ((dir (file-name-directory yeah-check--emacs))
         (candidate (expand-file-name "emacsclient" dir)))
    (or (and (file-executable-p candidate) candidate)
        (executable-find "emacsclient")
        candidate))
  "The emacsclient program that reaches the server.")

(defconst yeah-check--answer "live text"
  "The text the attached Emacs holds in the buffer of the check.")

(defvar yeah-check--hold-the-answer t
  "Whether the check holds the answer of the child until the bridge drains it.
The control of the claim of the determinism removes this one step: the
check then reads the buffer as it always did, the loss of the answer
is a race again, and the control of the bridge does not bite.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-chunk nil
  "The chunk of the child process that the filter has not delivered yet.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-filter nil
  "The filter of the bridge, kept to deliver the held chunk later.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-process nil
  "The process of the bridge, kept to deliver the held chunk later.")

(defun yeah-check--filter-of (args)
  "Return the filter of ARGS, or nil when ARGS names none."
  (let ((tail args)
        (filter nil))
    (while tail
      (when (eq (car tail) :filter)
        (setq filter (cadr tail)))
      (setq tail (cddr tail)))
    filter))

(defun yeah-check--without-filter (args)
  "Return ARGS without the :filter keyword and its value."
  (let ((rest nil)
        (tail args))
    (while tail
      (unless (eq (car tail) :filter)
        (setq rest (append rest (list (car tail) (cadr tail)))))
      (setq tail (cddr tail)))
    rest))

(defun yeah-check--around-make-process (orig-fun &rest args)
  "Create the process of the bridge, but hold what it prints.
The filter of the process keeps the chunk instead of handing it to
the bridge: the answer of the child reaches the bridge only when the
bridge asks for the pending output of a process that is gone."
  (let ((filter (yeah-check--filter-of args)))
    (if (and filter yeah-check--hold-the-answer)
        (progn
          (setq yeah-check--held-filter filter)
          (let ((process
                 (apply orig-fun
                        (append (yeah-check--without-filter args)
                                (list :filter
                                      (lambda (_process chunk)
                                        (setq yeah-check--held-chunk
                                              (concat yeah-check--held-chunk
                                                      chunk))))))))
            (setq yeah-check--held-process process)
            process))
      (apply orig-fun args))))

(defun yeah-check--around-accept-process-output (orig-fun &optional process &rest args)
  "Run the event loop of Emacs, and give the held answer to the bridge.
The answer of the child is delivered when the bridge asks for the
pending output of a process that is gone: the bridge reads the answer
of the child after its exit, which is the condition the defect is
about."
  (let ((result (apply orig-fun process (or args (list 0.05)))))
    (when (and yeah-check--hold-the-answer
               (null process)
               yeah-check--held-chunk
               yeah-check--held-filter)
      (let ((chunk yeah-check--held-chunk))
        (setq yeah-check--held-chunk nil)
        (funcall yeah-check--held-filter yeah-check--held-process chunk)))
    result))

(defun yeah-check--advise (symbol function)
  "Advise SYMBOL with FUNCTION.
Emacs 30 asks for the kind of the advice and the older Emacs does
not; the advice itself takes the original function as its first
argument in both."
  (if (>= emacs-major-version 30)
      (advice-add symbol :around function)
    (advice-add symbol function)))

(let ((failures nil)
      (name (format "yeah-bridge-keep-%d" (random 1000000))))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        (make-process
         :name "yeah-bridge-keep-server"
         :command (list yeah-check--emacs
                        (concat "--daemon=" name)
                        "--eval"
                        (format (concat "(with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create \"*yeah-live*\") "
                                        "(insert \"%s\"))")
                                yeah-check--answer))
         :connection-type 'pipe
         :noquery t)
        ;; wait for the server
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) 8)))
          (while (and (< (float-time) deadline)
                      (not (zerop (with-temp-buffer
                                    (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil
                                                  "-s" name "--eval" "t")))))
            (accept-process-output nil 0.1)))
        ;; the hooks of the check: the answer of the child waits for the
        ;; bridge to ask for the pending output of a process that is gone
        (yeah-check--advise 'make-process #'yeah-check--around-make-process)
        (yeah-check--advise 'accept-process-output
                            #'yeah-check--around-accept-process-output)
        (unwind-protect
            (let ((text (condition-case err
                           (let ((yeah-bridge-program yeah-check--emacsclient)
                                 (yeah-bridge-server name))
                             (yeah-bridge-buffer-read "*yeah-live*"))
                         (error (format "ERROR: %S" err)))))
              (unless (equal yeah-check--answer text)
                (push (format "the bridge lost the answer: it answered %S" text)
                      failures)))
          (advice-remove 'make-process #'yeah-check--around-make-process)
          (advice-remove 'accept-process-output
                         #'yeah-check--around-accept-process-output)))
    ;; stop the server
    (ignore-errors
      (with-temp-buffer
        (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil "-s" name "--eval" "(kill-emacs)")))
    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "bridge-keep: %s" failure))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el ends here

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; An explicit, permissioned bridge to the buffers of an attached
;; Emacs, reached through `emacsclient'.  The bridge is a capability
;; and not a convenience: the two tools carry their own names, so
;; the permission system can approve `bridge__eval' and
;; `bridge__buffer_read' separately, and nothing enters the tool
;; registry until the operator asks for it with `yeah-bridge-register'.
;;
;; The program is started with `make-process' -- never through a
;; shell -- and every call is bounded by a short timeout, so a busy
;; or absent server cannot hang the agent.

;;; Code:

(require 'yeah-tools)

(defgroup yeah-bridge nil
  "The Yeah emacsclient bridge."
  :group 'yeah)

(defcustom yeah-bridge-program "emacsclient"
  "Program used to reach the attached Emacs.
The program is run directly, without a shell, so it must be an
executable found on `exec-path' or the path of an executable file."
  :type 'string
  :group 'yeah-bridge)

(defcustom yeah-bridge-server nil
  "Name of the Emacs server the bridge connects to.
When nil, `emacsclient' connects to the default server.  A service
placement reaches a specific attached Emacs, so the name is a
capability: the operator names which Emacs the bridge may reach."
  :type '(choice (const nil) string)
  :group 'yeah-bridge)

(defconst yeah-bridge--timeout 2
  "Seconds a bridge call may take before its process is killed.")

(defconst yeah-bridge--probe "t"
  "Expression evaluated to find out whether the attached Emacs answers.")

(defun yeah-bridge--program-path ()
  "Return the path of the executable bridge program, or nil.
The program is not found when `yeah-bridge-program' is empty or
names a file that cannot be executed."
  (let ((program yeah-bridge-program))
    (and (stringp program)
         (> (length program) 0)
         (executable-find program))))

(defun yeah-bridge--trim (text)
  "Return TEXT without its trailing newlines."
  (let* ((text (or text ""))
         (end (length text)))
    (while (and (> end 0)
                (memq (aref text (1- end)) '(?\n ?\r)))
      (setq end (1- end)))
    (substring text 0 end)))

(defun yeah-bridge--stderr-text (buffer)
  "Return the text collected in the stderr BUFFER."
  (with-current-buffer buffer
    (buffer-string)))

(defun yeah-bridge--wait (process timeout)
  "Wait for PROCESS to exit, but no longer than TIMEOUT seconds.
Return non-nil when the process exited in time."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) timeout)))
    (while (and (process-live-p process)
                (< (float-time) deadline))
      (accept-process-output process 0.05))
    (not (process-live-p process))))

(defun yeah-bridge--run-program (path args timeout)
  "Run PATH with ARGS and collect what it printed.
Return a plist with the keys `:ok', `:status', `:output' and
`:message'; see `yeah-bridge--run' for their meaning."
  (let ((output "")
        (stderr-buffer (generate-new-buffer " *yeah-bridge stderr*"))
        (process nil))
    (unwind-protect
        (condition-case err
            (progn
              (setq process (make-process
                             :name "yeah-bridge"
                             :command (cons path args)
                             :connection-type 'pipe
                             :noquery t
                             :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                             :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                                       (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                             :stderr stderr-buffer))
              (yeah-bridge--wait process timeout)
              (let ((timed-out (process-live-p process)))
                (when timed-out
                  (ignore-errors (kill-process process)))

                ;; filter: the answer of the attached Emacs is then lost
                ;; and the bridge answers with nothing.  Draining the
                ;; pending events after the exit — until the output stops
                ;; changing — gives the filter its last words.
                (let ((previous nil)

                  (while (and (< (float-time) drain-deadline)
                              (not (equal previous output)))
                    (setq previous output)
                    (accept-process-output nil 0.05)))
                (let ((status (unless timed-out (process-exit-status process))))
                  (list :ok (and (not timed-out) (eq status 0))

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The bridge collects what the attached Emacs printed with a process
;; filter.  A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the
;; filter: the answer was then lost and the bridge reported success
;; with an empty output — the person saw an empty buffer that the
;; server had never emptied.
;;
;; The check used to race the subject: it kept a thread spinning to
;; make the parent late, read the buffer of the attached Emacs a
;; hundred and twenty times and failed only when the answer was
;; really lost.  Five runs of six bit and one did not (2026-11-16):
;; the claim came out `inconclusive' and the map came out `unknown'.
;; The check now commands the subject instead of racing it.  The
;; hooks it owns hold the answer of the child process until the
;; bridge asks for the pending output of a process that is gone —
;; the very condition of the defect — and the bridge must deliver
;; the answer all the same.  The same input gives the same verdict
;; every time, and the control of the claim (the drain of the bridge
;; removed) makes the check fail by its own assertion.

;;; Code:

(require 'yeah-bridge)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--emacsclient
  (let* ((dir (file-name-directory yeah-check--emacs))
         (candidate (expand-file-name "emacsclient" dir)))
    (or (and (file-executable-p candidate) candidate)
        (executable-find "emacsclient")
        candidate))
  "The emacsclient program that reaches the server.")

(defconst yeah-check--answer "live text"
  "The text the attached Emacs holds in the buffer of the check.")

(defvar yeah-check--hold-the-answer t
  "Whether the check holds the answer of the child until the bridge drains it.
The control of the claim of the determinism removes this one step: the
check then reads the buffer as it always did, the loss of the answer
is a race again, and the control of the bridge does not bite.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-chunk nil
  "The chunk of the child process that the filter has not delivered yet.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-filter nil
  "The filter of the bridge, kept to deliver the held chunk later.")

(defvar yeah-check--held-process nil
  "The process of the bridge, kept to deliver the held chunk later.")

(defun yeah-check--filter-of (args)
  "Return the filter of ARGS, or nil when ARGS names none."
  (let ((tail args)
        (filter nil))
    (while tail
      (when (eq (car tail) :filter)
        (setq filter (cadr tail)))
      (setq tail (cddr tail)))
    filter))

(defun yeah-check--without-filter (args)
  "Return ARGS without the :filter keyword and its value."
  (let ((rest nil)
        (tail args))
    (while tail
      (unless (eq (car tail) :filter)
        (setq rest (append rest (list (car tail) (cadr tail)))))
      (setq tail (cddr tail)))
    rest))

(defun yeah-check--around-make-process (orig-fun &rest args)
  "Create the process of the bridge, but hold what it prints.
The filter of the process keeps the chunk instead of handing it to
the bridge: the answer of the child reaches the bridge only when the
bridge asks for the pending output of a process that is gone."

# AGENTS.md — the entry point to this repository

> **Yeah** means **Yeah, Emacs Agent Harness**: a recursive acronym, the
> **Y** is the Y-combinator. The harness itself is
> Emacs Lisp; Emacs is not merely a client to an external agent. The model is
> reached through gptel, effects go through the tool registry and permission
> system, and session history is append-only JSONL.
>
> The long-term Y metaphor means bounded recursive delegation, runtime
> self-inspection and a fixed point where Yeah can develop and verify Yeah.
> These are goals, not assertions about today's prototype.
>
> This repository is governed by **math-coding v5**: `spec.json` holds the
> standing specification (`schema_version: 5`) and the claims, `waves/*.json`
> holds the historical work units, and evidence comes from checks bound by
> `mathc run`.  Version 4 is frozen and archived at `waves/spec-v4.json`;
> its evidence is not current.
> `docs/PLAN.md` defines the current target sequence; do not mistake an old
> wave number or a green module row for a working end-to-end feature.

## Read first, in this order

1. `README.md` — actual current status and explicit limitations.
2. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the normative target: purpose, ten decisions,
   contracts, security, placements and non-goals.
3. `docs/PLAN.md` — the detailed eight-stage execution plan and release gates.
4. `docs/ENGINEERING.md` — binding dependency, infrastructure, library,
   process, security, testing and packaging practices.
5. `spec.json` — the standing machine-checked specification.
6. `waves/*.json` — existing math-coding units, with intent, check, promise
   and objection.
7. `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md` — kernel Elisp conventions; §11 is the trap log.
8. `lib/yeah-*.el` — the implementation, one feature per file.

If two sources contradict each other, report the contradiction in the open
work item. Never resolve it by silently making documentation more optimistic.

## The commands

```sh
./scripts/dev help                  # the list of subcommands
./scripts/dev byte-compile-all      # kernel compiles clean, with no warnings
./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/*.el   # unit tests
./scripts/dev check tests/checks/*  # canaries bound to claims
./scripts/dev map                   # claims, states and uncovered surface
./scripts/dev run                   # execute checks and bind evidence
./scripts/dev gate                  # run, then map; exit code is the verdict
# Opt-in real model call; credentials come from the environment:
emacs -Q --batch -L lib -l tests/live/live-model-call.el
```

`scripts/dev` needs Emacs on `PATH` (or `EMACS`). Method commands also need a
compatible math-coding binary on `PATH` or in `MATHC`. A CLI/version mismatch
is blocked tooling, not a successful check.

Exit codes are: `0` pass, `1` fail, `2` blocked/input error and `3` unknown.
Unknown is never pass.

## The method

Start with the map when the compatible method binary is available:

```sh
./scripts/dev map
```

A claim has a scope, requirement, falsifier, register and **control**. The
control breaks the subject and must make the check fail by a real assertion,
not merely by making the test unreadable or crashing Emacs. A claim whose
control has not bitten is not established.

Two rules are not negotiable:

- **A check that cannot fail is a comment.**
- **Unknown is not pass.**

A placeholder that returns success is also a failed implementation. Public
scenarios must be tested end to end, not inferred from the presence of a
function or module.

<!-- math-coding:end -->

## Task recording for the Math Coding field pilot

This project takes part in a measurement of the method itself. A task that ends
with a handoff is recorded in the field lab; without that record the pilot has
no data and the method cannot be judged.

At the end of the task, create a draft — the machine fields are filled for you:

```sh
~/Projects/math-coding-field-lab/scripts/record draft yeah --kind <kind> --base <revision-at-task-start>
```

Fill the fields marked `TODO`: the model, the time, the counters. Leave `outcome`
as `pending` and `accepted_by` empty — the owner decides the outcome and records
the acceptance, and that is not the agent's call. Then write the record:

```sh
~/Projects/math-coding-field-lab/scripts/record commit yeah --task-id <id>
```

Rules: do not choose tasks by their result, do not rewrite a written record to
make it look better, and do not drop unsuccessful ones — the pilot publishes
every outcome. The lab records every task that starts after the declared rule:
it never stops asking and it never filters by result. If the lab is not
available, finish the task as usual: a missing record is a gap in the
measurement, not a reason to change the work.

## Working rules

- Follow the stage order in `docs/PLAN.md`; do not start ACP, placements or
  sub-agents ahead of their prerequisites.
- Every new claim needs a control shown to bite. Every feature needs an
  observable end-to-end check appropriate to its layer.
- `lib/` is Elisp only. No C, Rust or shell scripts inside the kernel.
- One feature per file; `(require 'yeah-x)` loads `lib/yeah-x.el`.
- Public symbols use `yeah-`; internal helpers use `yeah--` or the module's
  established internal prefix.
- Domain errors are `user-error` or structured tool errors, not false success.
- Use `let` for request-local dynamic configuration of special variables;
  use `setq` only for intended global/session mutation. See ELISP §11.1.
- Subprocesses use `make-process`, never blocking `shell-command` in tools.
- Interactive execution never waits by spinning the event loop.
- Run context, permissions and sessions must not leak through new global
  mutable state.
- No telemetry, secret logging, global default keybindings or global gptel
  mutation.
- Development-only Nix/mathc/research clones never become runtime dependencies.

The detailed rationale and additional rules are in `docs/ENGINEERING.md` and
`ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md`. Update documentation whenever behavior changes;
update `AGENTS.md` if the documented workflow itself changes.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
